title: refactor: consolidate generation cache lifecycle
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Centralizes cache keying, R2 lookup/replay, miss handling, and response capture in one shared lifecycle.
- Keeps media and text as separate adapters with their existing buckets, serialization, content checks, and streaming behavior.
- Adds /v1/images/generations to the shared media cache, resolves its seed once, and applies safety before constructing cache/public URLs.
- Preserves legacy OpenAI-image cache objects, fallback attribution, and only stores successful 200 text responses.
- Validated with TypeScript, Biome, and 39 focused cache, OpenAI-image, and safety tests.

Storage-neutral prerequisite for #13299.

gist.headline: One cache to tend them
gist.blurb: The generation cache got a proper shared greenhouse instead of several adjacent sheds. Image, audio, video, and text requests now follow one well-watered lifecycle.
gist.summary: Centralized generation cache keying, R2 replay, miss handling, and response capture across media and text, while adding shared cache support for OpenAI-compatible /v1/images/generations requests.
gist.impact: Repeated image-generation requests, including /v1/images/generations, can now reuse safely validated cached results with consistent seed handling, legacy cache compatibility, and unchanged text streaming behavior.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy shared cache greenhouse: several labeled garden pipes for images, text, audio, and video feed into one large lime-green storage jar, with old jars kept safely on a shelf for legacy compatibility. Polli should be a careful garden keeper using a tiny tool belt to connect the pipes, while the eager CRT Monitor Robot watches cached image tiles replay on its screen; small code-plants and flowers show that the separate adapters still grow independently.
